hints: Remember that relative atomic mass is a weighted average, so start by working out the percentage of the main isotope, $^{32}\text{S}$.
The $^{32}\text{S}$ makes up 93.0%, so set up the average as $(93.0 \times 32 + 4.2 \times 34 + 2.8 \times 36)$ divided by 100.
Calculate the total carefully and divide by 100, then round to one decimal place to see which value it is closest to.
walkthrough:
**Find the percentage of the main isotope**

The sample must add up to 100%. So the % of $^{32}\text{S}$ is what is left after the other two.

$$\% \, ^{32}\text{S} = 100 - 4.2 - 2.8 = 93.0\%$$

**Set up the weighted average for $A_r$**

$A_r$ is the average mass weighted by abundance. Multiply each isotopic mass by its percentage, add them, then divide by 100.

$$A_r = \frac{(93.0 \times 32) + (4.2 \times 34) + (2.8 \times 36)}{100}$$

**Calculate and round**

Work out each part calmly. This is where careful arithmetic pays off.

$$A_r = \frac{2976 + 142.8 + 100.8}{100} = \frac{3219.6}{100} = 32.196$$

**Give the final answer**

Rounded to one decimal place, 32.196 becomes 32.2. That matches the weighted average you expect, just a little above 32 because of the small amounts of heavier isotopes.

options.A: 32.1 is a little too low. It likely comes from an arithmetic slip, such as rounding down too early or miscalculating one of the small contributions from $^{34}\text{S}$ or $^{36}\text{S}$.
options.B: 32.2 is correct. Using 93.0% $^{32}\text{S}$, 4.2% $^{34}\text{S}$ and 2.8% $^{36}\text{S}$ gives (3219.6/100) = 32.196, which rounds to 32.2.
options.C: 34.0 is far too high. It ignores weighting and just averages the mass numbers (32+34+36)/3. $A_r$ must be close to 32 because 93% of the sample is $^{32}\text{S}$.
options.D: 34.3 is far too high. It may come from averaging only the two heavier isotopes or forgetting that $^{32}\text{S}$ is by far the most abundant and pulls the average down near 32.
